assertion: Sworn warrant application recited two recent failure-to-appear warrants and a history of interfering with and resisting law enforcement on three dates, as the stated basis for requesting an arrest warrant rather than a criminal summons.
record: Of six specific factual assertions, one is supported by the issuing court's own public docket. One cited date is an alias summons issued for a different named person; one date returns no entry; one cited arrest date returns no case; two cited dates correspond to peace disturbance and to stealing.
source_doc: Statement of Probable Cause; Case.net dockets 09AP-CR01193, 10AO-CR01779, 22AP-AC00335, 22AP-AC00335-01
generalizes_how: For a sample of warrant applications in a county, extract every factual assertion in the flight-risk and criminal-history sections and check each against Case.net. Report assertions supported / unsupported / attributable to another person. Inputs are public; the procedure is mechanical.
charitable_reading: The affiant wrote 'arrests,' not 'convictions'; a person may be arrested for one offense and charged with another. A records check keyed to a shared identifier (see HF-004) could produce a muddled history without any intent to mislead.
reform_hook: Affidavit certification standards; supervisory review before warrant application in misdemeanor cases
est_scale: Every warrant application in every Missouri county with Case.net coverage
next_action: Obtain certified copies of the four dockets; build the two-column check sheet as a reusable template

assertion: Information charging RSMo 574.207 alleges the defendant was warned to stay away and then approached an officer with intent to interfere.
record: RSMo 574.207 requires approach within twenty feet after a warning. The Information omits the twenty-foot element entirely.
generalizes_how: Pull all Informations charging 574.207 in a set of counties and measure how many plead the twenty-foot element. A defect rate per county and per prosecutor's office is a single table.
charitable_reading: Charging documents are often drafted from a form and amended on motion; omission may be routine practice rather than a substantive defect.
next_action: Identify whether Case.net permits charge-code search across counties for 574.207

assertion: An officer requested an arrest warrant rather than a criminal summons, on recitals that largely do not survive the court's own records (HF-001).
record: Warrant issued; bond set; a surety bond was posted. The surety premium is non-refundable regardless of outcome, so the discretionary choice of warrant over summons transferred money out of the defendant's pocket before any adjudication.
source_doc: Bond order; bondsman receipt and contract (to be obtained)
generalizes_how: For misdemeanor filings in a county, measure the warrant-versus-summons rate, then multiply warrants by the typical surety premium to produce a county-level figure for pre-adjudication cost imposed on defendants by a charging-officer's discretionary request.
charitable_reading: Warrant requests may follow a standard checklist that an officer applies uniformly rather than selectively.
reform_hook: Summons-preferred policy for non-violent misdemeanors; presumption against warrant where no prior FTA is verified
est_scale: All misdemeanor filings in a county per year
next_action: Obtain the bondsman receipt and contract; confirm the local premium convention

agency: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal history system
assertion: An Offense Cycle Number normally ties to a single arrest event.
record: One OCN appears on a 2009 charge in one court, a 2010 warrant service, and a 2010 charge in a different court.
generalizes_how: Sample OCNs appearing on Case.net charge records and count how many span more than one arrest event or more than one court. If the rate is non-trivial, any criminal-history recital keyed to OCN is unreliable at scale.
charitable_reading: Most likely a data-entry or display artifact in the public docket rather than in the underlying criminal-history record.
reform_hook: Criminal-history record accuracy; audit requirements for OCN assignment
est_scale: Statewide; affects every records check keyed to OCN
next_action: Test the pattern against unrelated public dockets to see whether it recurs

assertion: Pending — RSMo 610.100 request submitted for mobile video recordings of an incident at a nonpublic location.
record: Pending. Record the response, the exemption cited if refused, the fee charged, and the elapsed days.
source_doc: SEND-2 request and the agency's response
generalizes_how: Submit identical 610.100 requests to a set of Missouri agencies and measure response time, fee, exemption cited, and whether the nonpublic-location right of access is honored. This is the Missouri analogue of the Kansas KORA matrix.
charitable_reading: Small agencies may genuinely lack the staff to respond within the statutory window.
reform_hook: RSMo 610.100 response deadlines, fee caps, and retention
next_action: Send SEND-2 certified; log the date; calendar the statutory response window

agency: Jasper County Circuit Court, Associate Division
assertion: A party was defaulted twice for failure to appear.
record: The same docket records five Returned Mail-Undeliverable entries, including a Notice of Entry marked Unable to Forward, during the same window. Both defaults were later set aside on the party's motion.
generalizes_how: Scrape associate civil dockets for cases containing both a Returned Mail-Undeliverable entry and a subsequent default for non-appearance. The co-occurrence rate is pure docket arithmetic and needs no interpretation.
charitable_reading: Parties are obliged to keep a current address on file with the court; returned mail may reflect the party's own failure to update it.
reform_hook: Alternative service before default; mandatory re-notice where mail is returned undeliverable
next_action: Draft the docket-scrape specification; it can be built during quarantine

assertion: K.S.A. 45-218(d) requires a response within three business days; K.S.A. 45-219 limits fees to actual cost.
record: To be measured. Capture for each target: days to response, fee quoted, exemption cited, and whether the exemption matches the records withheld.
source_doc: KORA request copies and agency responses
generalizes_how: This is already the design of the KORA matrix. The harvest addition is to log each divergence as a numbered finding rather than only as a tracker row, so that individual refusals become citable.
charitable_reading: Agencies commonly miss the three-day window for volume reasons rather than to obstruct.
next_action: Add a finding_id column cross-reference to the KORA response tracker

assertion: Agency ALPR policies state retention periods, access controls, and audit-log requirements.
record: To be measured. Compare each agency's stated policy against the audit logs, retention settings, and sharing agreements actually produced in response to a records request.
source_doc: Agency ALPR policy; audit logs; interagency sharing agreements
generalizes_how: Policy-versus-practice comparison runs identically for any surveillance technology with a written policy and a machine-generated log. The instrument is technology-agnostic.
charitable_reading: A gap between written policy and vendor default configuration is frequently an oversight at procurement rather than a deliberate practice.
reform_hook: Statutory retention limits and mandatory audit-log disclosure for ALPR
est_scale: Every ALPR-operating agency in the state
next_action: Confirm the audit-log request language captures logs rather than policy only

assertion: RSMo 610.100 provides access to mobile video recordings, and agency retention schedules for such recordings are commonly short.
record: An indigent misdemeanor defendant is typically not appointed counsel until the initial appearance, which here falls roughly three weeks after the incident. Where a retention period is thirty days, the preservation window can expire at or near the moment counsel first appears.
source_doc: RSMo 610.100; agency retention schedules; the charging timeline in this matter
generalizes_how: Collect, for a set of agencies, the mobile-video retention period, and for a set of courts, the median interval from arrest to appointment of counsel. Where the first number is smaller than the second, the statutory right of access is structurally unavailable to indigent defendants.
charitable_reading: Retention periods are set by storage cost and by schedules that predate widespread body-worn camera use; the interaction may simply never have been considered.
reform_hook: Automatic preservation on arrest; extended retention where charges are filed; earlier appointment of counsel
est_scale: Statewide; every indigent misdemeanor defendant in a recorded encounter
next_action: Request the retention schedule itself as a public record — it is not case-specific and can be obtained now
